extracted.intended_audience: readers, contributors, and advertisers of The Forerunner (progressive women and potential magazine contributors/advertisers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluative standards for content, criticism, reader Q&A, and advertising for The Forerunner magazine (Charlotte Perkins Gilman). Covers what content the magazine seeks, how advertisements and endorsements are handled, and standards for ethical reader-submitted questions and expense-reporting advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portrayal of women as human, not merely mothers
rubrics_metrics.description: He sees women as females—and does not see that they are human; the universal mistake of the world behind us; but one unworthy of a mind that sees the world before us so vividly. He likes them as mothers. He honors them as mothers. He wants to have them salaried, as mothers. But he thinks it quite beyond reason that they should appear as regular members of the working world; their motherhood, to his mind, would prevent it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism expects authors to recognize that both sexes share the special qualities of the species and that women should be depicted as full human beings with interests and activities beyond motherhood; reviewers should call out portrayals that reduce women to only maternal roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid reducing women's motivations to mating/sexual impulse
rubrics_metrics.description: He overestimates the weight of this department of life, a mistake common to most men and some women ... dismisses all that passionate outgoing as comparable to the mating impulse of insects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers and critics should not attribute modern women's social unrest or ambitions solely to sexual/mating instincts; depict broader human drives (social, intellectual, civic) rather than analogies to insect mating behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character credibility and preservation of reader sympathy
rubrics_metrics.description: He has burdened himself with all this unnecessary complication of special foolishness on the part of his heroine which alienates our sympathy. Then he makes this girl, so strong and intelligent, deliberately refuse various kinds of work she might have done because they did not please her; and borrow money from a man in preference to earning her living. She exposes herself to insult and even danger with an idiocy that even a novel-reared child of sixteen would have scorned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characters—especially protagonists meant to elicit sympathy—should act in ways that are believable and justified by their situation; avoid gratuitous or implausible foolishness used merely to create plot complications or heroism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and depict the larger social/economic causes of women's unrest
rubrics_metrics.description: The painful exhibition of Mr. Wells's misapprehension of the larger causes of the present unrest among women. What later historians will point out as the most distinguishing feature of our time ... is the sudden and irresistible outburst of human powers, human feeling, human activities, and in that half the world hitherto denied such experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism and fiction should situate women's aspirations within social and economic contexts (e.g., movement toward economic democracy) rather than treating them as mere personal whims; show structural causes and consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magazine purpose: stimulate thought and offer practical solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: What is The Forerunner? ... It is to stimulate thought: to arouse hope, courage and impatience; to offer practical suggestions and solutions, to voice the strong assurance of better living, here, now, in our own hands to make.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content submitted to or published by the magazine should aim to provoke reflection, inspire action, propose practical remedies, and communicate a consistent humanistic/socializing outlook rather than mere entertainment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and tone of content (people, principles, everyday questions; male/female/child phases)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is about people, principles, and the questions of every-day life; the personal and public problems of to-day. It gives a clear, consistent view of human life and how to live it. It will treat all three phases of our existence--male, female and human. It will discuss Man, in his true place in life; Woman, the Unknown Power; the Child, the most important citizen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should address practical personal and public problems across sexes and generations, maintain a consistent human-centered perspective, and be relevant to daily life and social improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising must be truthful and based on personal knowledge/use
rubrics_metrics.description: In its advertising department, under the above heading, will be described articles personally known and used. So far as individual experience and approval carry weight, and clear truthful description command attention, the advertising pages of The Forerunner will be useful to both dealer and buyer. If advertisers prefer to use their own statements The Forerunner will publish them if it believes them to be true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred ad content is first‑hand endorsements and honest descriptions; the editor applies judgment about the truthfulness of advertiser statements and prioritizes personal recommendation and clear accurate description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertiser selection criteria and expectation of measurable value
rubrics_metrics.description: The value of this form of advertisement was not in the extent of the circulation, but in a. The unique and attractive method. b. The select class of goods. c. The select class of readers. d. The weight of a personal authority specially known to these select readers. If, however, the amount of sales secured does not equal the price of the advertisement, there is no reason whatever why any dealer should use our pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advertisers should supply select, well‑tested goods; expect targeted readership and personal-authority endorsements to drive measurable sales; the magazine reserves the right to evaluate ad effectiveness and decline further advertising if value is not delivered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial advertising policy and experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Forerunner offers to its advertisers and readers the benefit of this authority. ... The Forerunner will publish them if it believes them to be true. ... Meanwhile The Forerunner will continue to run one or two as samples; put in real ones when it gets them; and may find it necessary to take out the eight pages which would have been so useful if properly filled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The magazine may run sample or editorial-style ads, will move to paid ads when suitable, and may adjust the amount of advertising pages based on availability and suitability of truthful, personally endorsed products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Q&A / 'Personal Problems' editorial standard: no trivial or foolish questions
rubrics_metrics.description: The department of 'Personal Problems' does not discuss etiquette, fashions or the removal of freckles. Foolish questions will not be answered, unless at peril of the asker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reader Q&A should be substantive and practically important; trivial or frivolous queries are excluded; contributors answering must enforce this editorial standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expense-reporting ethics for official trips
rubrics_metrics.description: If the woman is required to send in an itemized account, she should do so, accurately. If her expenses are within the usual amount allowed it should make no difference to the employer whether the money is spent on a dinner or a theatre. She visibly could not suppress the theatre expense and yet have an accurate account; nor could she call it a dinner--and be truthful. If it is simply a matter of having such and such an allowance for expenses, then it is no one's business how she spends it; but if she has agreed to itemize she ought to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees must be honest in expense accounting: itemize when required; do not conceal or mislabel discretionary expenses; if given a lump-sum allowance, personal discretion is acceptable within the allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred product types for advertising (editorial wishlist)
rubrics_metrics.description: This is the list of articles the editor wishes to secure, having known and used them for from two to forty years; some were used by her mother before her. They are things you can buy anywhere or order by mail. [Long list: toilet preparation, courtplaster, silver cleaner, soaps, breakfast foods, soups, hairbrush, typewriter, pen, toothpaste, mattress, bookcases, music machine, fountain pen, dress shield, skirt-binding, etc.]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The magazine prefers advertising for proven, widely available household and personal products that the editor can personally endorse; advertisers offering such items are encouraged to contact the magazine.
